title: Divide a decimal by a whole number (7.2 ÷ 9)

lesson.title: Sharing 7.2 Fairly: Dividing a Decimal by a Whole Number

steps.say: You already know how to divide a number like seventy-two by nine. Today we just add a decimal point: nine friends are sharing seven point two metres of ribbon for a school project, so we need seven point two divided by nine.

Here is the secret. Seven point two is seven wholes and two tenths, which is the same as seventy-two tenths. So think of seven whole metres cut into tenths, plus the two tenths we already have. That gives us seventy-two little tenth-pieces to share.

visual.caption: 7 rods and 2 cubes: 72 pieces — but each piece is one tenth of a metre

steps.say: Now share those seventy-two tenths among the nine friends. Seventy-two divided by nine is eight, so each friend gets eight tenths. Eight tenths is written as zero point eight. So each friend gets zero point eight metres of ribbon.

visual.caption: 9 friends, 8 tenths each — 72 tenths shared with none left over

steps.say: When you write it the tall way, keep the decimal point in the answer directly above the decimal point inside. Seven ones will not make a whole group of nine, so we write zero in the ones place, then bring the two tenths along to make seventy-two tenths, and nine goes into that eight times. Zero point eight.

visual.caption: 0.8 is zero ones and eight tenths

steps.say: Here is the mistake to watch for. Some people just do seventy-two divided by nine and write eight. But stop and think: we only had seven point two metres of ribbon in total, so nobody can walk away with eight whole metres! The answer must be smaller than one. Losing the decimal point makes the answer ten times too big.

visual.caption: 0.8 sits close to zero — nowhere near 8

steps.say: So, turn the decimal into tenths, divide like you always do, and keep that decimal point right where it belongs.

lesson.answer: 7.2 divided by 9 is 0.8 — think 72 tenths shared 9 ways gives 8 tenths, and never lose the decimal point.

practice.question: Nine students at a Burnaby school share 4.5 litres of apple juice equally. Picture 4.5 as 45 tenths — that is 4 tens rods and 5 ones cubes of base ten blocks, where every block stands for one tenth of a litre. You can draw them if you like. How many litres does each student get?
practice.answer: 0.5 litres each. Forty-five tenths divided by nine is five tenths, and five tenths is written as zero point five.
